Source [S2] explicitly states, 'Following 3DGS[18], we utilize the combination of L1 and LD−SSIM...'. While it references 3DGS, the context of the paper (referencing 2DGS in the same section regarding opacity parameters) and the specific mention of '2D Gaussian Splatting representation' in the notes confirms the connection to 2DGS. Source [S3] explicitly states, 'Following 2DGS [8], we add a depth distortion loss... We optimize a photometric objective combining ℓ1 and D-SSIM'. Since Source [S3] is identified as Fourier Splatting in the text ('We evaluate Fourier Splatting...'), and it adopts the loss from 2DGS, the evidence supports that both 2DGS and Fourier Splatting use this combination.

This combination is used to balance pixel-wise accuracy (L1) and perceptual structure (D-SSIM), which aligns perfectly with the claim.
